messages:
sara.k: Heads-up — CI runner serviceaccount (build/ci-runner) tried to GET secrets in namespace 'customer-data' according to the audit alert. Not expected. Anyone else seeing cross-namespace secret reads?

jeff.m: seeing the same alert. pulling rolebindings now.

maria-r: quick hypothesis: last week's RBAC refactor introduced an aggregated ClusterRole that may grant secrets:view across namespaces. Will grep for recent ClusterRole changes.

sec-bot: kubernetes-audit: 2024-06-05T12:22:14Z GET /api/v1/namespaces/customer-data/secrets by system:serviceaccount:build:ci-runner (uid: sa-xxxxx). Anomaly score 0.86.

jeff.m: running these checks now:
```
# check effective permissions as that SA
kubectl auth can-i --as=system:serviceaccount:build:ci-runner get secrets --namespace=customer-data
# list clusterrolebindings referencing suspicious cluster role
kubectl get clusterrolebinding -o yaml | yq '.items[] | select(.roleRef.name=="agg-secrets-view")'
```

sara.k: immediate mitigation proposal: remove the SA from the ClusterRoleBinding (or patch the binding to remove the subject) and rotate the SA token. Also add a short-term admission webhook denylist for pods using that SA from accessing secrets in customer-data if we need extra guard.

oncall-security: I'm taking ownership for mitigation. Will remove the subject from the binding and rotate token. Posting steps I'm about to run.

oncall-security: 1) kubectl patch clusterrolebinding agg-secrets-binding -p '{"subjects": [ ... without the ci-runner ...]}'
2) kubectl delete secret $(kubectl get sa ci-runner -n build -o jsonpath='{.secrets[0].name}') -n build  # forces token reissue
3) run audit replay to enumerate data pulls since 12:00Z

maria-r: Found the refactor change: aggregate role "agg-secrets-view" was created by infra/2024-05-29 and a ClusterRoleBinding 'agg-secrets-binding' was added with subjects from multiple namespaces. That binding is what allowed cross-namespace access. I will open a revert PR for the refactor to remove aggregation.

jeff.m: after removal, verify:
```
kubectl auth can-i --as=system:serviceaccount:build:ci-runner get secrets --namespace=customer-data --no-headers
# expect: no
```

sec-bot: Audit review: only 3 GETs to secrets were observed, all by the ci-runner SA, no creations or updates. No evidence of exfil over external egress observed in first-pass flow logs. KMS decrypt logs: no unexpected decrypts outside normal CI times.

sara.k: good — still treat as sensitive. Action items (short):
- oncall-security: remove subject, rotate SA token, push emergency RBAC rollback PR (in progress)
- maria-r: revert aggregator creation + add unit tests to prevent cluster-scoped secret grants via aggregated roles
- jeff.m: run full audit replay + correlate with KMS decrypt logs and VPC flow logs; share manifests of any pods that used the SA
- sec-bot: create alert rule to detect cross-namespace secret reads by non-admin SAs

oncall-security: done removing subject and rotated token. PR for emergency rollback: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/482 (WIP). Will hold for 30m before merging to confirm no customer impact.

maria-r: adding follow-ups: add CI gating check that aggregated clusterroles can't include verbs on secrets unless explicit allowlist, and add a nightly audit job to report SA->namespace secret access patterns.

sara.k: agreed. We'll treat this as an incident for tracking — severity: S2 (sensitive read), no evidence of exfil but still an RBAC regression. Please add to incidents board and schedule postmortem after rollback.

jeff.m: I'll attach the audit replay results and a minimal repro (kubectl commands and YAML) to the incident ticket.

sec-bot: Note: added label incident:rbac-regression to thread and created ticket INC-2024-1127.

sara.k: thanks team. Once PR merges, let's run an org-wide search for any other aggregated roles created in the last 60 days and flag them for manual review.

oncall-security: merging PR now (merging -> revert agg role). Will monitor for any services that break and rollback if needed.

maria-r: I'll prepare a short remediation doc for product teams explaining why some CI jobs will need explicit namespace-scoped roles instead of relying on aggregator roles.

sara.k: closing loop — keep me posted on audit log changes and KMS decrypt logs; we'll reopen if anything suspicious turns up. :white_check_mark:
